targetText: In what relation do the Communists stand to the proletarians as a whole?
summary: Communists do not form a separate party opposed to workers; they represent the interests of the entire working class.
context: The Manifesto emphasizes working-class unity across different industries and nationalities.

targetText: single sentence: Abolition of private property.
summary: Communism seeks to abolish private ownership of productive assets (factories, land, mines), not personal possessions.
context: Marx clarifies the difference between personal items (clothes, homes) and private capital used to exploit labor.
